This is game 12 in a series of 9×9 Go games. Each new game starts in a fresh session.

## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

## What carries over

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If CLAUDE.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session; your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

Your working directory holds:
- CLAUDE.md (10,953 bytes)
- games.md (18,336 bytes)
- libs.py (813 bytes)

## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: your Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools, for any file in your working directory.

You also have a shell, and you may write and run code in it; Python is available as `python3`. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.

- Opening as White was too LOW: C4, F4, G3, B4, D4 all 3rd/4th line. Black's G6/D7/B6/H4 framed
  the top AND both sides; my answers (B4 to B5, D4 to C5, E5/F5/G4 to D6/E6/G5) were all

  move 6-8) while Black's top is still thin — e.g. W E7/F7 between D7 and G6 or a 3-3 at G8/C8

  placement + J6 hane + F7/F9 took both sides. Rule: an invasion behind a completed wall needs
  ~6 points of edge on BOTH sides; if the opponent can play the 1-2 point (H9) and the 2nd-line
  hane (J6) there is only one eye. Don't invade where the wall is already solid; invade earlier.
- Endgame: B A4 hane, W A3 atari (single stone, 2 libs) let B B3 ataris and take the whole
  A1-B3 corner (~6 pts). Answer an edge hane with the SOLID block (B3/A3 + connect) and keep
  the stone touching my wall; never leave a lone 2-lib stone on the 1st/2nd line.
- Tactic note: the huge Black group had only 4 libs at one point (A6,A7,E7,E9) and no eyes, but
  E7/E9 were shared with my 2-lib D8 group (= seki shape) and Black could always kill my one-eyed
  right group to gain libs. A one-eyed group of mine next to it is a lib source for them.

B F6, W G4, B G6, W C7 (invasion), B D7, W D6, B C6!, W E7, B E6 (captures D6), W D8, B D6,

Takeaways:
- GOOD: top-left kill tactics. C6 atari on the cutting stone, E6 capture, F7/F8 hane, E9 hane
  (forced W D9), then B9 placement made C8 a killing cut (W ignored -> C8, C9 took 4 stones).
  Pattern: when an enemy group is joined only through one empty point (C8) and that point is
  self-atari for me, first take the OUTSIDE liberty of the point (B9 removes C9's escape) and
  then the cut becomes a real capture.
- BAD: opening split. C4 / W D4 attach / B D5 hane / W E4 / B E5 / W C3 hane / B C5 (gote) /
  W F4 gave White ALL of rows 1-4 (36 pts) while I had rows 5-9 (45) minus everything White
  could live in. One surviving 8-pt White group (A5-C7 connected to B4 via A4) + losing H4/H5
  area = lost by ~18 even after killing 4 stones. As Black, a "rows 5-9 vs rows 1-4" split
  needs a perfect top; better answer to the D4 attach is to keep a bottom foothold (D3 hane
  underneath, or B3/C3 corner) so White's bottom is not a whole 4-row strip.
- BAD: the left White group B6-B8/C7/A5/A6 escaped by connecting at A4 to B4-B3-C3. I played
  B5 (move 33) but White then B3/B4 linked under it. B4 at move 33 (instead of B5) would have
  cut it from the bottom; the corner group had no eyes by itself.
- BAD: H4 hane stone had 2 libs after W H3; I tenukied (G3 invasion) and W H5 put it in atari
  -> lost H4 plus H5/J4/J5 (~5 pts). A hane stone at 2 libs must be connected (H5) before
  invading elsewhere (lesson 1 again!).
- Bottom invasion (G3/F3/E2/F2/G2/E1) died: 3 libs, eye space E1-G1 only, W H1/D1 took both
  ends. The white chain had only 2 libs (D3,H4) but both were unreachable (D3 suicide while
  D2/C3 white, H4 surrounded). Don't count liberties I can't legally fill.
# Usage: python3 libs.py <<< "board rows 9..1 as 9 lines of X/O/." ; prints groups and liberties
import sys
cols="ABCDEFGHJ"
rows=[l.split() for l in sys.stdin.read().strip().splitlines()]
rows=[r[1:10] if len(r)>9 else r for r in rows]
B={}
for i,r in enumerate(rows):
    for j,c in enumerate(r): B[(j,9-i)]=c
def nb(p):
    x,y=p
    for q in((x+1,y),(x-1,y),(x,y+1),(x,y-1)):
        if q in B: yield q
seen=set()
for p in B:
    if B[p] in"XO" and p not in seen:
        g=[p];libs=set();k=0;seen.add(p)
        while k<len(g):
            for q in nb(g[k]):
                if B[q]=='.':libs.add(q)
                elif B[q]==B[p] and q not in seen: seen.add(q);g.append(q)
            k+=1
        n=lambda s:",".join(sorted(cols[a]+str(b) for a,b in s))
        print(B[p],n(g),"libs:",len(libs),n(libs))
